system.name: Deneb
system.description: The brightest star in Cygnus and one vertex of the Summer Triangle, Deneb is an A2Ia blue-white supergiant roughly 2,600 light-years away. Despite its great distance it ranks among the brightest stars in the sky, powered by an intrinsic luminosity ~200,000 times that of the Sun.

deneb.name: Deneb
deneb.description: An A2 Ia blue-white supergiant and one of the most luminous stars in the Milky Way, radiating about 200,000 times the Sun's energy. Its distance is uncertain — estimates range from about 1,400 to 3,200 light-years — making Deneb one of the most intrinsically luminous stars visible to the naked eye.
deneb.funFact: If Deneb were as close to Earth as Sirius (8.6 ly), it would appear as bright as a crescent Moon and cast visible shadows at night.
